costGuide.title: Land Rover Puma 2.4 TDCi Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a Puma 2.4 TDCi typically takes 12-16 hours at £65/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes .
paragraphs: The primary cost driver for a Puma 2.4 TDCi engine replacement is the condition of the turbocharger and the fuel injection system. Units where the turbo oil feed pipe banjo bolt has been preemptively modified and the injector copper washers replaced command a slight premium but carry significantly lower long-term risk. Additionally, the mechanical simplicity of this engine means a full Puma 2.4 TDCi rebuild is generally more cost-effective than modern complex alternatives. failures.title: Land Rover Puma 2.4 TDCi Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Turbocharger Oil Feed Pipe Blockage (2007-2011)
items.whatHappens: The banjo bolt on the turbo oil feed pipe contains a fine mesh filter that degrades and blocks oil flow to the turbocharger. This leads to turbo starvation, shaft failure, and potential engine ingestion of debris if the turbo disintegrates.
items.repairVsReplace: Removing the mesh filter and fitting a solid banjo bolt is a critical preventative measure. If the turbo has already failed and sent metal debris into the sump, a full Puma 2.4 TDCi engine replacement is often the only viable solution.

items.title: Injector Seal and Copper Washer Degradation
items.whatHappens: The copper injector seat washers and O-rings degrade over time, allowing combustion gases and soot to build up around the injector base (often called "chuffing"). This leads to hard starting, misfires, and potential cylinder head damage if ignored.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the copper washers and seals is a routine and highly effective repair. If left ignored and cylinder head warping occurs, a full unit replacement is required.

items.title: EGR Cooler and Valve Leaks
items.whatHappens: The EGR cooler can develop internal cracks, leading to coolant loss into the exhaust or intake. The EGR valve itself can also stick open, causing rough running, loss of power, and excessive smoke.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the EGR cooler and valve is a standard repair. If coolant ingestion has caused hydro-locking or bearing damage, a full Puma 2.4 TDCi engine replacement is necessary.

failures.goodYearsLine: The 2.4 Puma is generally considered more robust than the preceding Td5 regarding head gasket failures, but the turbo oil feed pipe issue is a critical, well-documented weakness that must be addressed immediately upon purchase .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Puma 2.4 TDCi
variants.intro: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically visible near the dipstick tube, or listed on the VIN plate under the bonnet. The Puma 2.4 TDCi is frequently confused with its predecessor, the Land Rover Td5 (which is a completely different 2.5L engine with no common rail injection), or its successor, the Land Rover Puma 2.2 TDCi (which shares the same block but features a revised cylinder head, different injectors, and updated ECU mapping). Fitting a 2.2 TDCi into a 2.4 Puma vehicle requires ECU remapping, different injector coding, and altered engine mounts, making exact code matching critical to avoid costly installation errors.

relatives.description: - the mechanically distinct 2.5L predecessor, which lacked common-rail injection but is renowned for its simpler, more robust design and different failure profile.
- the 2011+ update that retained the same block architecture but featured a revised cylinder head, different injectors, and updated ECU mapping to meet stricter emissions standards.
- the Ford-sourced 2.2L Duratorq variant used in the Freelander 2 and Evoque, sharing similar common-rail architecture but with different mounting orientations and turbo plumbing.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement Puma 2.4 TDCi - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Puma 2.4 TDCi is only advisable for lower-value hosts or project builds, and must come with verifiable proof that the turbo oil feed pipe banjo bolt has been modified and the injectors have been recently serviced. Without this documented history, the risk of inheriting a starved turbo or chuffed injector seat is unacceptably high. Explore our vetted used Puma 2.4 TDCi engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned Puma 2.4 TDCi addresses the core weaknesses of this generation. It will include a modified solid turbo oil feed banjo bolt, new injector copper washers and seals, and a serviced turbocharger. This is the most sensible, cost-effective route for preserving a classic Defender without the unpredictability of a used unit. Compare reconditioned Puma 2.4 TDCi options

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-mileage examples showing signs of bore wear, or if the engine has already suffered turbo debris ingestion. A quality rebuild should include line-boring, new pistons and rings, and a complete overhaul of the fuel system to exceed factory specifications. Discuss a custom Puma 2.4 TDCi rebuild

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Our network of vetted UK Land Rover specialists can supply the unit and handle the complex installation, backing the work with a nationwide warranty so you have a single point of contact for the entire job. View supply and fit options
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: For typical host vehicles like the 2007-2011 Land Rover Defender 90/110, current market values vary wildly based on condition, ranging from £8,000 for rough, high-mileage examples to £25,000+ for pristine, low-mileage classics . With reconditioned replacement costs starting around £3,500, the replacement is generally financially viable for most Defender hosts. However, for lower-value or heavily modified examples, if the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing.

items.question: What is the most common failure on the Puma 2.4 TDCi?
items.answer: The dominant failure patterns on the Puma 2.4 TDCi are turbocharger oil feed pipe blockage, injector seal degradation, and EGR cooler leaks. The turbo oil feed pipe banjo bolt contains a mesh filter that can degrade and block oil flow, leading to turbo starvation and catastrophic failure. Injector copper washers degrade over time, causing combustion gas blow-by (chuffing) and hard starting. EGR coolers can crack internally, leading to coolant loss and potential hydro-locking.

items.question: Which Land Rover models use the Puma 2.4 TDCi engine?
items.answer: The 2.4L Puma TDCi was fitted exclusively to the final-generation Land Rover Defender 90, 110, and 130 models between 2007 and 2011. It was introduced to meet Euro 4 emissions standards while retaining the low-end torque required for serious off-road use. It is mechanically distinct from the preceding Td5 and the succeeding 2.2 TDCi. Always verify your specific chassis code before ordering a replacement unit.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned Puma 2.4 TDCi engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned Puma 2.4 TDCi is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the known age-related weaknesses of the turbo oil feed system and injector seals. Used units carry a high risk of inheriting a starved turbo or chuffed injector seats. Proper reconditioning proactively upgrades these specific weak points with a solid banjo bolt and refreshed copper washers. Reconditioned units come with a 12 to 24-month warranty, unlike the 3-6 months typical for used engines.

items.question: How do I know if my car has the Puma 2.4 TDCi and not the Td5 or 2.2 TDCi?
items.answer: You can confirm your engine code by checking the VIN plate under the bonnet or the stamped code on the engine block near the dipstick tube. The 2.4 TDCi is visually identifiable by its common-rail injection system and specific turbo plumbing, lacking the mechanical rotary pump of the Td5. It is commonly confused with the 2.2 TDCi, which features a revised cylinder head and different ECU mapping. Fitting the wrong revision will cause severe compatibility and mapping issues.
